industry: Gyms, fitness studios, boutique fitness, martial arts/kids activity programs
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Results guaranteed or your money back' (GOLD-gyms-fitness-054) unless the guarantee's conditions are clearly stated (16 CFR 239) and the results claim is substantiated
Weight-loss numbers ('Lose 20 lbs in 30 days') or before/afters with 'results not typical' disclaimers; disclose generally expected results (16 CFR 255.2)

'Founding member rate for life' / 'lifetime membership' (GOLD-gyms-fitness-042/043) in California, where lifetime health-studio contracts are prohibited (Civ. Code 1812.80+); elsewhere state the real terms ('locked while your membership stays active')
'Free' trials or '$1 join' that silently roll into paid memberships; 'cancel anytime' unless cancellation is genuinely simple
'Up to 50% off' (GOLD-gyms-fitness-025) unless a meaningful share of items/plans actually get the maximum discount (16 CFR 233)
Contest/prize promotions ('Biggest Winner', GOLD-gyms-fitness-064) without official rules; with purchase requirement they may become illegal lotteries
compliance_notes: Negative options (verified): FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel amendments were vacated by the 8th Circuit (July 2025). The pre-2024 Negative Option Rule is back (effective 2/12/2026) and covers only prenotification plans. FTC issued a new ANPRM on 3/13/2026 (comments closed 4/13/2026); no new rule yet. ROSCA still governs online sign-ups (clear terms, express consent, simple cancellation).

FTC v. LA Fitness (filed Aug 2025; amended Jan 2026) alleges cancellation made unreasonably hard; LA Fitness argues ROSCA doesn't apply to in-person gyms. Unresolved as of 2026-11-02 (verify before relying).

California health-studio law (verified via DCA): Civ. Code 1812.85 right to cancel by midnight of the 5th business day with refund within 10 days; contract terms max 3 years; lifetime contracts prohibited. California ARL (B&P 17602, amended by AB 2863 for contracts on/after 7/1/2025): express consent, clear disclosure, online cancellation where sign-up was online, notices before price changes and free-trial conversions.
Many other states have health-club/'health spa' statutes (cooling-off periods, bonding, term limits); not verified per state tonight.
Endorsements and results (16 CFR 255, 2023 Guides): before/after and member testimonials imply typical results; 'results not typical' won't cure; disclose what members generally achieve.
Guarantees (16 CFR 239): state conditions and how to claim; 'money-back' must be honored as stated.

Sweepstakes/contests by mail (39 USC 3001(k)): 'no purchase necessary' and 'a purchase will not improve your chances' clearly and conspicuously, plus rules, odds and prizes. Skill contests also need clear rules.
Kids' programs: children's photos only with parent written consent; no data collection from children under 13 online without verifiable parental consent (COPPA) for QR landing pages.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold set 'founding member for life' (GOLD-gyms-fitness-042/043) vs California's ban on lifetime health-studio contracts
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: 'locked while your membership stays active' everywhere, never lifetime contracts in CA.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Before/after transformation cards (GOLD-gyms-fitness-054) vs FTC 255 typical-results rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: allowed only with generally expected results disclosed; outcome-feeling photos are the default.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: MMR-011 premium restraint (Equinox) vs discount-heavy mass gym cards
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Not a rule conflict: match the client's positioning. Patrick's votes will settle tone defaults when they exist.
